findings.statement: CA9 is the top convergence gene: RNA is up in tumour vs normal [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312] and protein is confirmed [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]. It replicates in TCGA-KIRC and survives purity extrapolation (tumour-intrinsic), and has antibody (girentuximab) and small-molecule history.

Safety caveat for CA9 as a therapeutic target: the GTEx vital-organ proteome flags it as enriched in stomach [gene=CA9; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.19], above the TS>=4 concern threshold. It is better as a tissue/imaging biomarker than as a payload target. It also has no prognostic signal in TCGA and no ccRCC-selective dependency.

CD70 is strongly up at protein level [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421] and RNA [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.464]. It replicates in TCGA-KIRC, is tumour-intrinsic after purity correction, and has clinical-stage antibody/ADC programmes (cusatuzumab, vorsetuzumab). It is a leading membrane-target candidate, not prognostic and not a DepMap dependency.

ENPP3 is a tumour-up membrane enzyme with protein support [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544] and a larger RNA change [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.895]. It is ranked 6th in the target profile, replicates in TCGA and has an ADC (AGS-16C3F, phase 2).

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile (tumour-up, protein-confirmed [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.837], purity-robust, TCGA-replicated, Open Targets genetic association). However, it is enriched in a vital organ (adrenal) in the GTEx proteome [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08], a safety concern, and it has no drugs or selective dependency.

NNMT is up at protein level [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], is tumour-intrinsic and replicates in TCGA. Higher expression predicts worse survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], making it a prognostic biomarker candidate. It is an intracellular enzyme, so a small-molecule rather than antibody strategy applies.

Negative result: FCER1G is up in bulk tumour (rank 16 convergence) but tracks immune infiltration. Its RNA correlates negatively with purity [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692] and the change shrinks in a pure tumour [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061]. TYROBP behaves similarly, so these are immune-cell signals and not tumour-cell targets.

PSAT1 is the top biomarker-profile gene and is down in tumour at protein level [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963]. Higher expression is associated with worse overall survival in TCGA [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.43], so it is a prognostic tissue biomarker, not a target (down-regulated).

UMOD shows loss of normal tubule identity, with a massive RNA drop [gene=UMOD; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-10.31], replicated in TCGA. Similar strong down-regulation is seen for SLC12A1, ALDOB and SLC22A8. These are diagnostic or lineage biomarkers, not targets.

SLC16A3 (MCT4, lactate exporter) is up in RNA [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.435], with protein support, a cis copy-number effect and purity robustness. It is a Warburg-metabolism membrane target, though it has no drug history here and no selective dependency in ccRCC lines.

VHL is the disease-mechanism anchor: 3p copy-number loss is frequent [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791] and the gene is significantly recurrently mutated in the combined cohort. Its own RNA/protein change is modest, so it is a driver and not a differential-expression target.

caveats: Evidence is bulk CPTAC (110 tumours) plus TCGA RNA replication; no independent protein validation.
The GTEx vital-organ proteome has no kidney and a limited detection range; absence is not safety.
No candidate shows a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap/PRISM, and 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology.
Rankings are heuristic; robustness intervals for lower-ranked genes are wide.
Literature and PubMed context were not queried; only omics-layer evidence is reported.
